title: Hypoparathyroidism and Pseudohypoparathyroidism: Albright Osteodystrophy, GNAS and PTH Resistance

steps.title: Biochemical Hallmarks of Hypoparathyroidism
steps.tx: True hypoparathyroidism features hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, and inappropriately low or undetectable serum intact PTH in the presence of normal renal function. Establishing the **Biochemical hallmark of hypoparathyroidism** reveals that without parathyroid hormone, distal renal tubular calcium reabsorption fails while proximal tubular phosphate excretion is severely diminished. Impaired renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase activity reduces calcitriol synthesis, compounding intestinal calcium malabsorption.
steps.say: Primary hypoparathyroidism is characterized by low calcium and elevated phosphate alongside inappropriately low intact parathyroid hormone.

steps.title: DiGeorge Syndrome 22q11.2 Microdeletion Pathology

left.title: Pharyngeal Pouch Dysgenesis
points: Defective 3rd and 4th pharyngeal pouch migration
Aplasia or hypoplasia of parathyroid glands
Thymic hypoplasia with cellular T-cell immune deficiency

right.title: Cardiofacial Phenotype
points: Conotruncal cardiac defects (tetralogy, truncus arteriosus)
Cleft palate, velopharyngeal insufficiency
Dysmorphic facies with micrognathia and low-set ears

steps.tx: Congenital hypoparathyroidism occurs in up to 60% of infants with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (DiGeorge) due to defective 3rd and 4th pharyngeal pouch embryogenesis, accompanied by conotruncal cardiac defects and thymic hypoplasia. Recognizing **DiGeorge syndrome 22q11.2 deletion** is vital because neonatal hypocalcemic convulsions or tremors are frequently the initial presentation. Fluorescent in situ hybridization or chromosomal microarray confirms the microdeletion.
steps.say: DiGeorge syndrome from a twenty-two q eleven microdeletion produces neonatal hypoparathyroidism, thymic hypoplasia, and conotruncal cardiac defects.

steps.title: Clinical Signs of Neuromuscular Hyperexcitability

left.title: Chvostek Sign
points: Tapping facial nerve anterior to external auditory meatus
Ipsilateral twitching of facial muscles (angle of mouth, eye)
Elicited by heightened peripheral nerve excitability

right.title: Trousseau Sign
points: Inflating BP cuff 20 mmHg above systolic pressure for 3 min
Induces painful carpopedal spasm with thumb adduction
Higher sensitivity and specificity than Chvostek sign

steps.tx: Latent hypocalcemia is elicited by Chvostek sign (facial nerve tapping producing ipsilateral facial muscle twitch) and Trousseau sign (carpopedal spasm induced by inflating BP cuff 20 mmHg above systolic for 3 minutes). Testing for **Chvostek and Trousseau signs of tetany** demonstrates how low extracellular calcium destabilizes neuronal membranes by reducing depolarization thresholds. Trousseau sign carries superior diagnostic accuracy, as Chvostek twitching can occur in healthy children.
steps.say: Latent hypocalcemia is revealed through Chvostek facial nerve twitching and Trousseau carpopedal spasm upon blood pressure cuff inflation.

steps.title: Emergency Parenteral Calcium Gluconate Resuscitation

left.title: Calcium Gluconate 10%
points: 1-2 mL/kg (100-200 mg/kg, max 10 mL)
Dilute equally with normal saline or D5W
Slow infusion over 10 minutes

right.title: Monitoring and Precautions
points: Continuous ECG rhythm monitoring
Halt infusion if bradycardia develops
Avoid calcium chloride due to extravasation necrosis

steps.tx: Acute symptomatic hypocalcemia (seizures, laryngospasm) requires immediate IV 10% calcium gluconate (1-2 mL/kg or 100-200 mg/kg, max 10 mL) infused slowly over 10 minutes under continuous ECG monitoring. Administering **Emergency acute tetany calcium gluconate** avoids calcium chloride due to severe extravasation necrosis. Continuous electrocardiographic monitoring is required during infusion to detect bradycardia, PR prolongation, and lethal ventricular arrhythmias.
steps.say: Acute hypocalcemic seizures or tetany require slow intravenous calcium gluconate over ten minutes under continuous cardiac monitoring.

steps.title: Pseudohypoparathyroidism Type 1a PTH Resistance

nodes.label:
Maternal GNAS Mutation
Loss-of-function on maternal allele

Defective Gs-alpha Protein
Impaired receptor coupling

Renal Tubular Resistance
PTH fails to activate renal cAMP

PHP-1a Phenotype
Hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, high PTH

steps.tx: PHP-1a features target-organ resistance to PTH: hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia with markedly elevated PTH, caused by maternally inherited heterozygous loss-of-function GNAS mutations. Investigating **Pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1a (PHP-1a) PTH resistance** reveals that because the renal proximal tubule exhibits tissue-specific maternal GNAS expression, maternal inheritance silences G-alpha signaling. Resistance extends to other G-protein coupled receptors, causing subclinical hypothyroidism and blunted growth hormone release.
steps.say: Pseudohypoparathyroidism type one a features parathyroid hormone resistance with elevated PTH due to maternal GNAS gene mutations.

steps.title: Albright Hereditary Osteodystrophy Somatic Phenotype

left.title: Craniofacial and Stature Features
points: Short stature with early growth plate fusion
Rounded moon facies with depressed nasal bridge
Centripetal childhood obesity and cognitive impairment

right.title: Skeletal and Ectodermal Findings
points: Shortening of 4th and 5th metacarpals (brachydactyly type E)
Dimpling over knuckles upon fist clenching (Archibald sign)
Subcutaneous osteomas and soft tissue ectopic ossification

steps.tx: AHO somatic phenotype consists of short stature, rounded moon facies, obesity, subcutaneous ossifications, and characteristic shortening of the 4th and 5th metacarpals/metatarsals (brachydactyly type E). Diagnosing the **Albright hereditary osteodystrophy (AHO) phenotype** is supported when knuckle dimpling replaces normal prominence over shortened metacarpals upon making a fist (Archibald sign). Subcutaneous nodules represent de novo dermal bone formation independent of circulating calcium levels.
steps.say: Albright hereditary osteodystrophy displays short stature, round facies, obesity, ectopic ossifications, and short fourth and fifth metacarpals.

steps.title: Pseudopseudohypoparathyroidism and Genomic Imprinting

rows: Severe (high PTH, high TSH, low calcium)

steps.tx: Paternally inherited GNAS mutations cause PPHP: patients inherit the identical AHO physical phenotype (brachydactyly, short stature) but maintain completely normal serum calcium, phosphate, and PTH due to tissue-specific maternal imprinting. Differentiating **Pseudopseudohypoparathyroidism (PPHP) paternal GNAS** inheritance shows that because renal tubular cells selectively express the maternal GNAS allele, the intact maternal copy maintains unhindered hormonal responsiveness. Thus, endocrine laboratory values remain entirely normal.
steps.say: Paternal GNAS mutations cause pseudopseudohypoparathyroidism, exhibiting physical Albright features without any endocrine resistance.

steps.title: Chronic Maintenance Therapy and Calcium-Phosphate Targets

left.title: Pharmacological Regimen
points: Oral calcitriol 20-40 ng/kg/day active vitamin D
Elemental calcium 30-50 mg/kg/day divided doses
Maintain low-normal serum calcium (8.5-9.0 mg/dL)

right.title: Renal Safety Surveillance
points: Prevent hypercalciuria (urine Ca/Cr < 0.2)
Avoid calcium-phosphate product > 55 mg²/dL²
Periodic renal ultrasound to screen for nephrocalcinosis

steps.tx: Maintenance therapy uses oral active vitamin D calcitriol (20-40 ng/kg/day) and elemental calcium carbonate (30-50 mg/kg/day), maintaining serum calcium in low-normal range (8.5-9.0 mg/dL) to prevent hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis. Achieving the **Chronic therapy goal (calcium-phosphate product)** with calcitriol and calcium carbonate requires vigilance because intact PTH is absent and renal calcium reabsorption is minimal, creating a profound risk for nephrocalcinosis if serum calcium is normalized too aggressively. Monitoring urinary calcium and renal sonography is mandatory.
steps.say: Long-term therapy uses calcitriol and oral calcium, keeping serum calcium low-normal to avoid hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis.
